card.title: BackOnTrack: posture-monitor firmware
card.result: I wrote all of the firmware (15/15 commits) for a four-person course team's wearable posture monitor: modular FreeRTOS/ESP-IDF on an ESP32-S3, with a real-time rule-based classifier (good posture + 5 fault states) that classified 95 of 100 live movements correctly in an informal check.
card.contextNote: EE/BIOEN 461; team: Sparsh, Matthew, Parneet, Ella
also: EE 474 labs (bare-metal ESP32-S3 GPIO, timer and PWM; ISRs, I2C and a priority scheduler; a FreeRTOS SRTF scheduler on a dual-core ESP32-S3).

card.title: SmartCrib: on-device cry detector
card.result: Joint project with Jonathan Lu. PDM mic → MFCC → INT8 TensorFlow Lite Micro model running fully on-device on an Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense (Cortex-M4), with an ESP32 alert bridge over BLE.
also: EE 446 TinyML compression work (INT8 quantization, pruning, distillation; magic wand, human-activity recognition, keyword spotting).

card.title: TPT-Finder bioimpedance instrument (BioZ v4)
card.result: A tetrapolar bioimpedance board, BioZ v4 (AD5933, INA333, AD8606 Howland current source). On the earlier BioZ v2 I calibrated the sensing chain to 0.034% error at 33 kHz (2200 Ω calibration), and I ran the ex-vivo study and all 500+ tissue measurements.
card.contextNote: UW BioRobotics Lab; my role: Biomedical Instrumentation & Impedance Lead
also: a two-electrode bioimpedance pen (AD5934), and support for the ultrasound and photonics sub-modalities.

card.title: Project SHIELD: sensor DAQ board and stress-test rig
card.result: An ESP32-S3 data-acquisition board for a design with 8 sensor types, plus the Faraday cage and orbital-shaker automation that stress-test it for SHIBench.
card.contextNote: Guide Air Labs capstone: co-hardware lead (with Thomas Glass) and procurement lead; ARC Lab: stress-test campaign lead

links.label: Project SHIELD: sensor DAQ board and stress-test rig

also: [`Faraday-Cage-design-`](https://github.com/sdadhich04/Faraday-Cage-design-): my 3D-printable cage, as Onshape CAD exports (STL and STEP).
`shaker-table-test`: the Python runners that drive the shaker table (described on the SHIELD page).
`Project_Shield_PCB`: zipped KiCad project versions of the board.

card.title: Real-time EMG BCI
card.result: I built a real-time EMG cursor BCI end to end: EMG streaming, a Kalman-filter closed-loop cursor, and a feedback-lag sweep.
card.ack: Built for EE 466 (Winter 2026) at UW in a three-person lab group with Jonathan and Olivia, following the course protocol and script outlines by A. L. Orsborn. The code here and the lag-sweep analysis are my own.

links.label: Real-time EMG cursor BCI with a feedback-lag sweep

card.title: EngineerGraph: a local evidence engine
card.result: A knowledge graph (7,170 nodes, 22,325 edges) over 46,472 indexed files that links 316 skills to the files and commits that prove them. It uses hybrid BM25 + vector search, and I cut a search from 1,604 SQL statements to 14 (0.4 s) with the ranking proven identical. The suite has 702 tests passed + 7 skipped.
also: Computer Vision Robotics Intern, Central Research Laboratory, Bharat Electronics (Aug–Sep 2025).

card.title: Signal processing inside SmartCrib and TPT-Finder
card.result: The DSP work sits inside two featured projects: the MFCC front end that feeds SmartCrib's INT8 model, and the sensing-chain calibration and impedance analysis at 33 kHz behind TPT-Finder's 0.034% error (measured on BioZ v2).
card.contextNote: SmartCrib: joint project with Jonathan Lu; TPT-Finder: UW BioRobotics Lab
also: EE 242 Fourier and audio signal-processing labs (eight Jupyter notebooks).

card.title: LEGv8 CPU in SystemVerilog
card.result: A LEGv8 processor built up from an ALU and a single-cycle datapath to a 5-stage pipeline with forwarding and a cache hierarchy.
card.contextNote: EE 469; team project with Ankith and Alexander Vuu
also: EE 271 digital-logic labs in SystemVerilog for the DE1-SoC (multiplexers, seven-segment display, FSMs, button debouncing, LFSR).

card.title: Sensing & control (no robot yet)
card.result: I haven't built a robot. The pieces I'd bring to one come from other projects: Kalman-filter state estimation in a closed loop (EMG BCI), IMU sensing with a BNO085 (BackOnTrack), automated test rigs (the SHIELD orbital-shaker sequencer), and CAD for a 3D-printable Faraday cage.
